name: Trading Post
owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-10: 'farm products pay the early game on a declining price. AFK-farmable food must not pay for everything -- cap it or exclude it.' SUPERSEDED 2026-10-13 (ECONOMY_V2 section 7, E3): 'No cap: farming is allowed. The Trading Post buys at fixed spine prices with no allowance.'

decisions.E1: cobble at its spine worth, not 1 P a stack: 64 cobblestone is the stone_earth crate
decisions.E2: two ways to sell: a crate of one category (exact, the v1 path) or 'sell everything I can' (a bounded take of whole crates, every category, and every specimen by the piece)
decisions.E3: no cap and no allowance. The v1 schedule (price by badge x crates per leg, $3,600 a player over the campaign) and the leg/spent/closed gates are REMOVED, not set high: tools/produce_buyer.py has no allowance code, the pack has no cob_pb_leg or cob_pb_sold score, and a crate pays its spine worth at every badge. The v1 rows are kept under superseded_schedule
decisions.E8: a Trading Post at every town square that already has a market (data/markets.json counters) and at the ports among them (Pacifidlog, Sunset Harbour, Viltri Quay each already have a counter), and Hollin's farm stays
decisions.E10: no co-op pooling: each sale is the seller's own purchase of their own inventory (the pack holds no shared state)

mechanism.summary: a Cobblemon dialogue NPC (tools/compile_dialogue.py's Compiler, as the ferryman: tools/ferries.py conversation()) whose options each run a sale function as and at the player. A crate sale refuses a second submit inside a cooldown, counts the crate's items (`clear @s <item> 0`), refuses when short, reads the balance (`cobbledollars query @s`), TAKES exactly the crate (`clear @s <item> <count>`) and, unless exactly the crate was taken, records the taken share of the price as owed and stops; then PAYS through the macro `$cobbledollars give @s $(amount)` and re-reads the balance: unless it rose by exactly the price the price is recorded as owed (score cob_pb_owed) and the player told to show an operator. 'Sell everything I can' reads the balance once, then for every category counts the player's items, divides by the crate size, TAKES that many whole crates with a bounded take (the macro `$execute store result score #took cob_pb run clear @s <item> $(n)`, which reports how many it removed) and credits crates x price; then for every specimen takes every piece (`clear @s <item>`) and credits pieces x price; then pays the total ONCE and re-reads the balance as above
mechanism.rung: functions (CLAUDE.md principle 6, rung 6 of 9). The rungs before it do not suffice: Cobblemon has no sell-back; the CobbleDollars bank (configuration) pays one global whole-dollar unit price, so it cannot price a unit below $1 (a stone is $0.1875) or take whole crates only (data/bank.json mechanism, 'cannot price below $1 a unit'); a datapack sells nothing; a vanilla villager's offers are per villager and cannot hold 64 stone for $12 across 16 sites without 16 villagers' worth of restock state. The same mechanism as the v1 buyer, which EXP-061 has not yet run
assumed: `clear <player> <item> 0` reports the number of matching items without removing any (vanilla behaviour, ASSUMED: EXP-061 step 3 tests it). If it removed them, the count step would take the goods with no payment

`clear <player> <item> <max>` removes at most max matching items and reports the number removed, and `clear <player> <item>` removes every match and reports the number (vanilla behaviour, ASSUMED, ECONOMY_V2 U2: untested here)

a macro line `$execute store result score ... run clear @s <item> $(n)` run through `function ... with storage` substitutes an NBT int as plain digits (vanilla 1.20.2+ macros, ASSUMED: tools/arena_runtime.py proves the same substitution for `cobbledollars give`)
`cobbledollars query @s` returns the balance as the command's result (EXP-040, relayed by tools/ferries.py)
`cobbledollars give @s <n>` adds exactly n (VERIFIED from the jar per tools/arena_runtime.py's comment; NOT run in game by this pack)

spine.rule: worth($) = count x W(tier) / rate_per_hour, rounded to a whole dollar per crate (ECONOMY_V2 1.1); 1 P = $100. W(tier) is the typical hour of data/bank.json effort_model.tiers, computed by tools/bank.py tier_hours() at build time (early $620, deep $1,350, nether $2,120 when this was written, MEASURED from the bank's own rates), never copied here. Every rate_per_hour below is the design's ESTIMATE (ECONOMY_V2 2.2, U3) until someone times an hour
spine.specimen_rule: price = W(early) / (ko_per_hour x the item's best per-defeat drop chance among the species that spawn in our world), rounded, at least $1 and at most cap_p x $100 (ECONOMY_V2 2.2 'Specimens')

kitchen_pharmacy.status: built 2026-10-14 (unit B2 finish; the owner: 'kitchen and pharmacy goods must be sellable'). NOT run in game (EXP-061). Every price below is DERIVED, never typed: `python tools/produce_buyer.py goods` re-derives it from this section and `check` fails when a crate drifts from it
kitchen_pharmacy.rule: ECONOMY_V2 2.2's crafts rule. A good's worth = (its inputs' worth + step) / the recipe's yield; step = max($2, 1% of the inputs) per craft, so a craft that yields several shares it. An input's worth is, in order: a unit of the crate that already buys it; a unit of a sold good here (what the post pays for it); a raw input's class below; or the cheapest recipe that makes it (an intermediate carries NO step: only a sold good does, so a chain never compounds a step the player did not pay for). A slot that accepts several ids takes the cheapest. The good is sold as a crate of the smallest n in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) whose price reaches crate_floor_dollars, the price rounded DOWN to a whole dollar. rate_per_hour on each kp crate is back-solved so that count x W(tier) / rate is that price: the independent audit (tools/economy_audit.py tp_expected) then reads these crates like any other, with no special case. A good that a live wild Pokemon also drops is worth no more than its drop (W / (ko_per_hour x chance))

harvest.why: one interaction per unit: break a planted crop, pick a berry, milk a Miltank (data/cobblemon/pokemon_interactions/miltank.json in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.2+1.21.1.jar: an empty bucket gives a milk bucket with cooldown 0, read 2026-10-14). The crops crate's own rate (crates[crops].rate_per_hour), ESTIMATE (U3) like it. The fastest known hand route sets the worth, so the price is never above the effort

dig.why: bulk digging by hand: the stone_earth crate's rate (crates[stone_earth].rate_per_hour), ESTIMATE (U3). Sand and snow are used only as INPUTS here: they are never sold (sand is a spawn-condition block, data/spawn_blocks.json)

drop.why: an item only a wild Pokemon drops: W(early) / (ko_per_hour x the best per-defeat chance among live species), the Specimens rule (docs/research/notes/drops-1.8.0.json). Chicken, cow and bee are on the mob blacklist (server/config/mods/mobsbegone-blacklist.json:6,13,15), so an egg and a honey bottle have no farm route

minecraft:milk_bucket.why: milked from a Miltank (or a female Gogoat, Skiddo or Bouffalant) with an empty bucket: miltank.json in the 1.8.2 jar, cooldown 0. Cows are blacklisted. The bucket comes back from a craft that uses the milk (ASSUMED, as the vanilla cake recipe returns it). If a recipe consumed the bucket, milk would cost the player more than priced here, so every good made with it would be priced at or under its real cost: the safe direction

minecraft:snowball.why: dug from snow with a shovel

minecraft:raw_gold.why: mined: the bank buys it at $20 (data/bank.json), the spine's own price for gold; a nugget is a ninth of an ingot

not_sold.cobblemon:smoked_tail_curry: its recipe needs cobblemon:tasty_tail and cobblemon:galarica_nuts; neither has a source in our world (no live dropper in docs/research/notes/drops-1.8.0.json, and no recipe), so it cannot be crafted and a price would have no derivation

not_sold.minecraft:cake: a placed cake is a spawn-condition block (data/spawn_blocks.json): paying for the item strips encounters out of the world (the same rule that keeps sand out of the crates; ECONOMY_V2 2.3)
not_sold.cobblemon:candied_apple: an apple's cheapest route is leaf decay in a tree farm, which has no rate on the spine; the drop route (W / (60 x 1.5)) would be dearer than that route and so overpay. Left unsellable rather than guessed

greeting: Trading Post. Posted price for anything you dig, cut, grow or catch, and no limit on how much. Sell a crate at a time, or I take everything I buy. Found items (held items and evolution items) go by the piece, and cooked dishes and medicines by the small crate, but only when you sell everything: that takes every potion, revive and dish you are carrying, so put away what you mean to keep.

messages.nothing: Nothing here that I buy, or not enough of any one thing for a crate.
messages.short_note: One take came up short of the count. You were paid for what was actually taken.
messages.take_failed: Something went wrong taking the crate. Nothing was paid; what was taken is recorded as owed to you (cob_pb_owed). Tell an operator.
messages.pay_failed: The money didn't arrive. It is recorded as owed to you (cob_pb_owed): tell an operator.
